We have 60 acres total.  
One-third is clay-rich: \( \frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20 \) acres.  
The rest is good soil: \( 60 - 20 = 40 \) acres.  

Good soil yield: 400 bushels per acre.  
Clay-rich yield: half of good soil, so \( 400 \div 2 = 200 \) bushels per acre.  

Yield from good soil: \( 40 \times 400 = 16000 \) bushels.  
Yield from clay-rich: \( 20 \times 200 = 4000 \) bushels.  

Total yield: \( 16000 + 4000 = 20000 \) bushels.  

Final answer: 20000
